Title: Fundamentals of Differential Equations, Eighth Edition

Author: R. Kent Nagle

Chapter: 7.3

Question: 2

Because of the linearity property of the Laplace transform, [;\mathcal{L}\{3t^2-e^{2t}\}=3\cdot\mathcal{L}\{t^2\}-\mathcal{L}\{e^{2t}\};].

Using the fact that [;\mathcal{L}\{t^n\}=\frac{n!}{s^{n+1}};] (from a table), [;\mathcal{L}\{t^2\}=\frac{2!}{s^{2+1}}=\frac{2}{s^3};].

Using the same table, we know that [;\mathcal{L}\{e^{at}\}=\frac{1}{s-a};]. So, [;\mathcal{L}\{e^{2t}\}=\frac{1}{s-2};].

Substituting these back into the original expression, [;\mathcal{L}\{3t^2-e^{2t}\}=3\cdot\frac{2}{s^3}-\frac{1}{s-2}=\frac{6}{s^3}-\frac{1}{s-2};].

Therefore, [;\mathcal{L}\{3t^2-e^{2t}\}=\frac{6}{s^3}-\frac{1}{s-2};].
